title: Head Coach Mike Macdonald: "I'm Proud Of Our Style Of Play"
headline: Price and Charbonnet could both return this week, Charles Cross's ankle is being taken day to day with no IR talk, and Rashid Shaheed's role is expected to grow.
summary: Macdonald said the offense's turnaround came from refocusing on the team's identity, specifically the run game, third downs, and style of play, while red zone finishing remains a point of emphasis. He praised the defense's connected effort and said the staff manages extra prep days carefully, since overloading the week has led to mental fatigue. He described Nick Emmanwori's growing versatility, noting he splits time between the defensive backs room and other position groups and handles the extra workload without frustration. On injuries, he said Charles Cross has an ankle injury with no timeline yet, that IR has not been discussed, and that the staff is taking it day by day. Rashid Shaheed's early returns are positive with no new update. Velus Jones Jr. has a hamstring injury of unknown severity. Macdonald said Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet could both play, but declined to give a benchmark for Charbonnet. He said Shaheed's usage can expand, especially through the return units. He also credited George Holani's third-down pass protection and the offensive line's play, and called Byron Murphy II's interior work the starting point for the defensive front.

topics.detail: Macdonald praised his consistency and maturity while he bounces between the DB room, Chris Partridge, and Zach Orr's room, with the coach saying the extra workload requires responsibility and extra time.

Byron Murphy II's interior play is the starting point for the defense, and Tyrice Knight has been productive when given opportunities behind Drake Thomas, with Macdonald expecting a high level from the linebacker corps regardless of who plays.
The team has Tuesday off, uses an extra day on Wednesday as a recovery day, and the coach is wary of overloading the week mentally.
Macdonald discussed working with a new offensive coordinator for the third straight year and said communication and partnerships with Jay Harbaugh and Aden Durde drive the process.
